It replaces printed posters and static signs with displays you manage remotely. It gives you full control over what appears on every screen, across locations, devices, and screen groups, without physical access to the screens. A waiting room TV is a screen in a patient waiting area that plays video, health information, and practice updates while people wait. In healthcare settings – doctors’ offices, dental practices, and clinics – the right content can calm patients, answer common questions, and make the wait feel shorter. This guide covers what to play, what to avoid, and how to run the screen so it stays useful and appropriate for a medical setting. What Should You Play on a Waiting Room TV? Use a balanced mix of patient education, practice information, and calming visuals. Each item should work without sound: Patient education clips – short explainers on procedures, conditions, and aftercare build trust and answer common questions. Practice information – services, hours, insurance accepted, new providers, and staff introductions help patients know what to expect. Health tips and seasonal reminders – flu shots, screenings, hydration, and allergy-season advice give people a useful reason to look up. Calming visuals – nature, an aquarium, or slow scenery can help create a calmer atmosphere. Local weather and controlled clinic updates – steady, useful information without breaking news, political content, or loud audio. Light, positive entertainment – trivia, did-you-know facts, and short, rights-cleared clips keep the mood easy. Queue or “now serving” information and simple wayfinding – use non-identifying numbers or codes only, never patient names or appointment details. Patient Education That Builds Trust Patient education often does the most work. The Calendar Widget lets you easily display upcoming events and schedules on your digital signage screens. By integrating with platforms like Google Calendar, Microsoft Outlook, or a Custom Source, you can automatically sync and showcase events in real time—saving time and improving visibility. This guide will walk you through how to import, customize, and style your calendar to match your design and scheduling needs, ensuring a smooth and efficient setup. How to Set It Up Add the Calendar Widget Drag and drop the Calendar Widget onto your canvas. A setup window will automatically appear. Select the Calendar Source Choose where your calendar data will come from. You can select one of the following options: Google Account Microsoft Outlook Account Custom Calendar (via CSV link or API) Importing Your Calendar Choose the source you’d like to import your calendar events from: Google Calendar Select Google Account. A sign-in window will appear—log in with your Google credentials to connect and sync your calendar. Microsoft Outlook Calendar Choose Microsoft Outlook Account. You’ll be prompted to log in with your Microsoft credentials to import events directly from your Outlook calendar. Custom Calendar If you’re using a different calendar system, select Custom Calendar. You’ll have two options to connect: CSV Link Enter the URL of your CSV file. How to set it up: In your calendar system, export or generate a CSV link (not a downloaded file, but a live URL) Copy the CSV URL In NoviSign Studio, paste the link into the CSV Link field Click Test (if available) to verify the data is loading correctly Save your settings Tip: If the file is password-protected, enable the “Account Login” option and enter your credentials.
